name: GLM-5.3 Flash

performance.note: Fused mHC improved decode throughput by 25.6% and reduced decode latency by 20.4% against an identical-geometry eager control. The Frontier performance thresholds pass, but the broader certification gates remain outstanding.

description: Text-only GLM-5.3-Flash Frontier candidate using Red Hat AI's NVFP4 experts, SparkLab's FP8 KDA projection format, native NoPE MLA/KPool, mHC, and NVMe-MoE serving.
limitations: The complete pinned checkpoint passed FTW index validation and end-to-end API serving; the artifact contains 1,634 entries across 23 shards.

Routed experts retain Red Hat AI's NVFP4 values. SparkLab additionally stores the bandwidth-dominant KDA q/k/v/o projections in per-output-row FP8 W8A16; recurrent gates, DSA projections, shared experts, embeddings, and output head retain source precision.
The fused-mHC probe measured 6.271 tok/s and 5.681 s warm TTFT, passing the Frontier performance thresholds, but its fixed response ended at the token limit before a final answer.
Prompt-selected expert rows must still be read from NVMe when absent from the GPU cache; these compulsory reads dominate TTFT.
FlashInfer 0.6.15's SM12x route packer exceeds Triton's tensor-size limit at 288 experts, so this recipe uses SparkLab's native Triton NVFP4 backend.
KPool sparse selection is currently eager and CUDA graph capture is disabled.
Multimodal certification is a separate later gate.
